decision_table.name: Determine_NC_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file North Carolina state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in NC (office, employees, property)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
NC filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
A corporation has physical presence nexus in NC if it has: - An office, store, warehouse, or other place of business in NC - Employees working in NC - Tangible personal property located in NC - Real property located in NC
Reference: NC General Statute § 105-130.4 (Nexus and apportionment) Reference: NC Department of Revenue Directive CD-98-1 (Nexus standards)

actions.action: // Economic nexus established per Wayfair - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
NC filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair).
Economic nexus threshold: $100,000 gross receipts OR 200 transactions in NC.
Following South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018), NC requires filing if a corporation exceeds economic nexus thresholds, even without physical presence.
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: NC Department of Revenue Economic Nexus Guidance Reference: NC General Statute § 105-164.8 (Economic nexus provisions)

No NC nexus - no filing requirement.
Corporation does not meet physical presence or economic nexus thresholds. Any estimated payments would be refunded.
Reference: NC General Statute § 105-130.4 (Nexus requirements)

decision_table.name: Calculate_NC_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate NC state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
NC state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
NC ADDITIONS to federal taxable income include: - Interest income from U.S. government obligations (exempt federally, taxable to NC) - IRC Section 199A qualified business income deduction addback (NC does not conform) - State income taxes deducted on federal return - Bonus depreciation addback (varies by tax year) - Expenses related to exempt income
NC SUBTRACTIONS from federal taxable income include: - Interest on NC state and municipal bonds - NC net operating loss deduction (subject to NC limitations) - Dividend income eligible for NC dividend received deduction - Certain refunds of state income taxes
Reference: NC Form CD-405 Schedule A (Additions to Federal Taxable Income) Reference: NC Form CD-405 Schedule B (Deductions from Federal Taxable Income) Reference: NC General Statute § 105-130.5 (Adjustments to federal taxable income)

No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.
Corporation does not have NC nexus, so no income adjustments are needed.

decision_table.name: Calculate_NC_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate NC state corporate income tax. Applies NC 2.5% flat rate to apportioned and adjusted taxable income. NC has the LOWEST state corporate tax rate in the nation.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
NC state corporate income tax calculation:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to NC: × [NC apportionment percentage] 3. NC additions: + [Federal interest, IRC 199A addback, etc.] 4. NC subtractions: - [NC municipal interest, NC NOL, etc.] 5. NC taxable income: = [Result] 6. NC tax rate: × 2.5% (LOWEST STATE RATE IN THE NATION) 7. NC income tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. NC credits: - [Jobs, film, renewable energy, historic preservation, etc.] 9. NC tax liability: = [Final tax]
NC uses single-sales factor apportionment (100% sales factor).
NC tax rate history: - 2025+: 2.5% (lowest in the nation) - 2019-2024: Various rates ranging from 2.5% to 6.9% - Before 2019: Progressive rates up to 6.9%
NC provides various tax credits including: - Article 3J: Jobs creation tax credit - Article 3F: Film and entertainment production credit - Article 3B: Renewable energy tax credit - Article 3H: Historic rehabilitation tax credit
Reference: NC Form CD-405 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: NC General Statute § 105-130.3 (Tax rate of 2.5%) Reference: NC General Statute § 105-130.4 (Single-sales apportionment) Reference: NC Department of Revenue Corporate Tax Bulletin 2025

No NC nexus - no tax liability.
Corporation does not have physical presence or economic nexus in NC. Any estimated payments are refunded.
Reference: NC General Statute § 105-130.4 (Nexus requirements)

No NC taxable income - no tax liability.
Corporation has NC nexus but no positive taxable income after apportionment and adjustments. Any estimated payments are refunded.
NC net operating loss (NOL) rules may apply: - NC allows NOL carryforward for 15 years - No carryback allowed (as of 2025) - NOL limited to 80% of taxable income (similar to federal)
Reference: NC Form CD-405 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: NC General Statute § 105-130.8 (Net operating loss deduction)
